title: incident-bot: oncall runbook autodiagnostics workflow enhancements
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: on-call engineers spend time context-switching during incidents to find the right runbook and relevant diagnostics. This PR enhances incident-bot's runbook autodiagnostics workflow by improving runbook suggestion relevance, adding automatic diagnostic triggers from the SLO toolkit, and surfacing compact actionable summaries to on-call in Slack and the Console. Changes include: - Runbook ranking: add a lightweight ranking scorer that considers SLO correlation signals, recent pager history, and matched symptoms (new feature flag 'runbook_ranking_v2'). - Autodiagnostics triggers: incident-bot subscribes to SLO-toolkit alerts and kicks off targeted diagnostic runs (heapsearch, request-rate histograms, recent error traces) when SLO degradation is detected. - Compact summaries: generate a short diagnostics summary (3 bullets) and attach runbook quick-links; summaries are stored as a compact blob in the incident metadata for faster retrieval. - Opt-in policy & rollout: new Team setting to opt into automated diagnostics; rollout staged via feature flag and 10% canary by default. - API/telemetry: added GraphQL mutation incident.autodiagnostics_run and telemetry events incident.autodiag.started/completed/failed to enable observability and cost accounting. - CLI: incidentctl supports --autodiag to force a run and --autodiag-dryrun for validation. - Docs: updated redwood-docs/runbooks and incident-bot README with configuration and example runbooks. Implementation notes: - Core ranking implemented as a thin scorer in incident-bot; scoring logic is feature-flag guarded and unit-tested. - Autodiag tasks are implemented as background jobs with idempotency keys to avoid duplicate runs during noisy alerts. - Diagnostic tooling hooks reuse existing slo-toolkit fetchers to avoid data duplication. - Storage: compact summary stored in incidents.metadata.autodiag_summary (kept intentionally small to avoid storage bloat). - Security: autodiag jobs only run for teams with opt-in; runbooks that include remediation steps require the 'oncall:execute' permission. Tests & CI: - Unit tests for ranking, telemetry, and job orchestration added. - Integration tests simulate an SLO violation and assert autodiag pipeline end-to-end (mocked external services). - One flaky test related to histogram aggregation flaked on CI and was fixed by adjusting timeout and stronger assertions; CI required a rerun before merge. Rollout & migration: - Default off for all customers; teams can enable via Console or incidentctl. - Migration includes a lightweight index rebuild for recent incidents to populate score hints; script provided in tools/incidents/reindex_autodiag_hints.sh. - Monitoring: added SLOs for autodiag latency and success rate; dashboards pre-created in observability-pack. Checklist: - [x] Feature flag gating implemented - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Docs updated - [x] Telemetry events instrumented - [x] Security review for opt-in policy done Related work: ENG-2145 implements the ranker prototype; SRE-317 covers SLO-toolkit alert wiring. Impact: improves mean time to mitigation for common SLO degradations by surfacing targeted diagnostics and runbooks faster. See Release Notes below for customer-facing summary.

review_thread: Jordan Lee: Nice work on the scorer. Left a few nits around the scoring weights and a suggestion to make the weights configurable per-team.
Aisha Patel: Thanks Jordan — weights are now configurable via team config and default to conservative values. Added tests for config parsing.
Ravi Malhotra: Can we ensure autodiag jobs don't leak secrets when posting summaries to Slack? Also requested an explicit permission gate.
Aisha Patel: Added permission check (oncall:execute) and scrubber for any secrets in runbook outputs. Updated docs to call this out.
Marta Gomez: Integration tests look good. One CI run failed due to histogram timeout; can you bump timeout and re-run?
Aisha Patel: Increased timeout and tightened assertions — re-ran CI and all checks passed.
